I have to stop here at least once a month to satisfy my cravings for the Italian Combo (Italian Beef & Sausage) with Mild Peppers on Italian Bread. What makes this sandwich so irresistible is the Sausage is browned before slow cooking it with the Roast Beef. The meat is then placed on the bread and generously drizzled with the juices from the slow cooker (Au-jus). The only thing I might suggest would be purchasing Italian loafs that have been fermented a bit longer for a crispier crust, but that's just me being picky. All in all these sangwitches (Chicago for Sandwich) remind me of the Italian Combo's served up at Chicago Cubs, Wrigley Field Ballpark, only $10.00 cheaper :)

Jimmy's Red Hots in Chicago's Humboldt Park neighborhood is among the most iconic, Chicago-style hot dog destinations that not only continues to thrive, but has stayed true to the classic, 312 fixings and generous portions that many of us have come to love. I have even heard celebrities reference this place as their favorite Chi-Town dog in our Windy City.

Great value. Consistent flavor. Open for over 55 years. The only changes that I noticed in a decade are the slight increase in menu prices (on par with inflation) and the heat-insulated, carryout bags that keep the dog and the fries hot (WHICH ARE STILL A COMPLIMENTARY ACCOMPANIMENT LIKE THE OLD DAYS). Now every fast-food vendor sells fries a la carte and will charge you extra for additional condiments such as Tzatziki (cucumber sauce) for that authentically flavored Gyro.

To this day, I love that Jimmy's refuses to add ketchup, or catsup depending on your hometown, to any of their hot dogs. They have maintained this position as a form of divine doctrine. If you want ketchup, you are welcome to ask for some "for your fries," but be prepared to be shunned by locals and workers for such debauchery if caught.

Thank you for staying the same Jimmy! Every time I stop in for a dog, polish or gyro, your place takes me back 20 years because of the nostalgic flavor and aromas.

Are you a fan of hot dogs? Do you live in Chicago or are visiting? Well Hot Doug's is THE place to go for hot dogs in the city. Sure there are a ton of smaller places and chains that can create a good hot dog experience in the city and surrounding suburbs. Quite a few of these other locations are great too but no one can touch the pure taste explosion that is Hot Doug's.

It's a gourmet hot dog disguised as a regular dog. I can't even recommend just one that you have to try because all of them are equally as good! From the classic Chicago-Style to the Polish to the Italian Sausage to the spicy variety - they have you covered.

Not only that but the dogs also are going to give you a side of fries. If it's Friday or Saturday (Honestly the two days you should be going) It's a side of fries FRIED IN DUCK FAT! (Fun fact: Duckfat makes EVERYTHING taste better. If they made them this way everyday.. .. Oh how a man can dream!)

If their regular menu isn't interesting enough though they also have specials! Hot dog specials made with all kinds of meat that rotate weekly. Animals you would never previously have thought would fit in sausage form that delight and amaze the taste buds! (I'll be honest when I used to go all the time I usually tried for 1 special + 1 other dog with no fries unless it's Friday or Saturday with the duck fat fries. I have no doubt that future visits will mimic this.)

My stomach and wallet are so happy that they aren't within walking distance of my office and that my friends that lived a few blocks away moved. (My taste buds crave that they are closer though!)

As all successful places in Chicago that do American food to perfection you are going to experience the one downside to the place - a long line. Still chatting with friends, strangers, or sitting on your cell phone will get you through it quicker as long as you don't focus on the delightful smells coming from behind the counter.

The building is quite large with a prominent signboard making the impression of inviting anyone to be able to come there. No need to dress up luxuriously or order in advance. Typical of a fast food restaurant. In the parking lot, I saw many cars that were still on both sides of the restaurant. Several cars were seen queuing in the drive thru section. there are also three men who are smoking near a large ashtray beside the restaurant, while occasionally looking inward, maybe a sign that he is a visitor in the same restaurant.

When we’re inside, the aroma and the warm atmosphere ambushed into both of our senses. I even hummed the songs they played. Those are 80s songs! It was like time machine and brought you into the era of Duran-Duran, Air Supply, to Jackson Five’s era.

The tables are also quite relaxed. Adjacent, but not crowded. Warm, but does not look pushy. Designed with red and white square, probably a standard unit for Portillo. Not too loud music makes visitors comfortable to talk, while there is still a loud laugh can be heard.

The menu choices on display are also simple. Strikingly colorful, but still with one theme. There are sections for burgers, salads, and beer that can be enjoyed by visitors. For operational reasons, only the first floor remains open until one o'clock in the morning. But that is not a problem, because the chair you want to occupy can be easily found. We chose a table near the window.

Mentioning the name of Portillo's, it means you are like being ready to be in a room with a true Chicago treat. For people who are trying it for the first time like me, this is a sign that we will be faced with several menu choices that want to be tried immediately. Without thinking twice, we chose their ultimate menu, hot dogs.

While waiting for the order, I circled my eyes to the whole room. Many frames or memorabilia hung on the walls that were deliberately made without the use of coatings, there were only red bricks there. Neat.

The visitors who came were mostly 25-50ish, employees who had just returned from work, and old partners. This is not a place for small families, because there is no baby chair there. My guess is, if I arrive early, then I won't get a place on this ground floor, because many people will fulfill it.

When the hot dog reached my hand, it was a plain hot dog, in a good way. There was no sauce, mustard, or mayonnaise between the piles of vegetables, pickles and soft bread that was still warm. The employees said the sauce and mustard would destroy the hot dog taste. A glass of coke is the perfect complement.

The smell of warmed bread can still be felt even though I have finished eating it. I want to try a combination of hot dogs, salads, and local beer that is sold there, with other friends, one day. Because of the bus arrival schedule, we finished the remaining food in hurry.

Finally, I asked permission to go to the lavatory to check -it was my habit to check the cleanliness of a restaurant- the hygiene, which was located on the second floor, and as you might guess, I had to use the elevator, which was quite annoying. But that feeling is then gone, because the state of the restroom is clean, and friendly to disabled visitors. Toilet paper uses two rolls, not just one. Hand sanitizers are also placed near the sink. Interestingly, there is no smell of urine or strong odor typical of fast food restaurants. I say thank you to the janitor.

My experience in Portillo is still cloudy due to time constraints. But I convinced myself to go back to exploring each menu, tasting every aroma of food served, and also the local beer that I had not had time to try. As an exchange student living in Illinois, at least I need to know a cool place to hang out, with friendly prices, open late into the night, and an easily accessible location when in downtown. Portillo's answered all my wishes.

Portillo's is so good! My husband and I tried it today for the first time. We ordered online for pick-up. Our food was ready 1 minute after the estimated time so the wait wasn't bad.

The char-grilled Maxwell Street Polish sausage was fantastic! The bun was substantial enough to support a big piece of sausage. The sausage had a good bite, without being too crunchy. The caramelized onions went perfectly with the mustard.

We ordered the Italian beef sandwich without peppers. After a 20-minute car ride in Wisconsin in January, it was still superb. The meat jus had lightly soaked into the bread, but it wasn't too soggy. The beef had great flavor!

The chicken tenders were pretty good. Not the best I've had, but not bad. Just not as amazing as the other entree options. The chipotle ranch dipping sauce, however, it absolutely marvelous. It has enough heat to be interesting, without being overwhelming.

The burgers are really big. We got a double bacon cheeseburger. It was really good. They burgers are char-broiled so it was very juicy.

The crinkle cut fries are perfectly. They are definitely a must have. They taste fabulous and are very crunchy. You can even order them well done.

Absolutely get a chocolate cake shake. It's such an interesting consistency and tastes so good! The vanilla milkshake is awesome as well.

Updated to add, the parking lot was packed at noon on a Sunday, but we were able to park at the mall and walk across the street to Portillo's.

Are you a fan of hot dogs? Do you live in Chicago or are visiting? Well Hot Doug's is THE place to go for hot dogs in the city. Sure there are a ton of smaller places and chains that can create a good hot dog experience in the city and surrounding suburbs. Quite a few of these other locations are great too but no one can touch the pure taste explosion that is Hot Doug's.

It's a gourmet hot dog disguised as a regular dog. I can't even recommend just one that you have to try because all of them are equally as good! From the classic Chicago-Style to the Polish to the Italian Sausage to the spicy variety - they have you covered.

Not only that but the dogs also are going to give you a side of fries. If it's Friday or Saturday (Honestly the two days you should be going) It's a side of fries FRIED IN DUCK FAT! (Fun fact: Duckfat makes EVERYTHING taste better. If they made them this way everyday.. .. Oh how a man can dream!)

If their regular menu isn't interesting enough though they also have specials! Hot dog specials made with all kinds of meat that rotate weekly. Animals you would never previously have thought would fit in sausage form that delight and amaze the taste buds! (I'll be honest when I used to go all the time I usually tried for 1 special + 1 other dog with no fries unless it's Friday or Saturday with the duck fat fries. I have no doubt that future visits will mimic this.)

My stomach and wallet are so happy that they aren't within walking distance of my office and that my friends that lived a few blocks away moved. (My taste buds crave that they are closer though!)

As all successful places in Chicago that do American food to perfection you are going to experience the one downside to the place - a long line. Still chatting with friends, strangers, or sitting on your cell phone will get you through it quicker as long as you don't focus on the delightful smells coming from behind the counter.

The Italian beef sandwiches are also good but my ultimate favorite are the burgers. Remember back in the day when places like Burger King would actually flame broil their burgers on-premises? Want to relive those days? Try a single or double burger at Portillo’s.

They also have fantastic tamales here - we used to get our girls tamales when they were little - now they mostly eat the chicken tenders like all little girls but I will occasionally get a tamale for myself - they’re tasty and fairly large.

The Trick to the Fries - Why the Hot Dogs, Hamburgers, & Beef are So Good

Portillo’s has the best Chicago Style Hot Dogs, Italian Sausage, Italian Beef, hamburgers, fries, and salads. Nothing else comes close.

Here's why the hotdogs taste so good. Vienna Beef worked with Dick Portillo years ago to create these hot dogs that can only be found at Portillo’s. The flavor is great but when you bite in there is almost a crunch. They aren't soggy like other places.

Just the regular fries are great but here are the tricks. First for a bit more ask for the "cheese fries" with mild cheddar cheese to dip them in. You can also ask for the fries to be "well done" so that they have this great crunch to them. The best.

The hamburgers are so good because they are cooked over an open flame to have a cookout taste. The special Milano Buns are so good, not like anything you can buy at the store. The Bacon Cheeseburgers are amazing. The Italian Beef is served on real Milano Rolls.

Most locations also have "Barney's Ribs" which are consistently good. The Chop Salad, Poppy Seed Fruit, and Mediterranean Salads all have chicken and are excellent healthy options.

The Chocolate Shakes are handmade with chocolate syrup. The Chocolate Cake Shake has, you guessed it, real chocolate cake in it. The Chocolate Cake is so good you will want it for your next birthday cake.

Everything is fresh and clean. There is always a line but it moves fast. Great place to bring kids.

The Trick to the Fries - Why the Hot Dogs, Hamburgers, & Beef are So Good

Portillo’s has the best Chicago Style Hot Dogs, Italian Sausage, Italian Beef, hamburgers, fries, and salads. Nothing else comes close.

Here's why the hotdogs taste so good. Vienna Beef worked with Dick Portillo years ago to create these hot dogs that can only be found at Portillo’s. The flavor is great but when you bite in there is almost a crunch. They aren't soggy like other places.

Just the regular fries are great but here are the tricks. First for a bit more ask for the "cheese fries" with mild cheddar cheese to dip them in. You can also ask for the fries to be "well done" so that they have this great crunch to them. The best.

The hamburgers are so good because they are cooked over an open flame to have a cookout taste. The special Milano Buns are so good, not like anything you can buy at the store. The Bacon Cheeseburgers are amazing. The Italian Beef is served on real Milano Rolls.

Most locations also have "Barney's Ribs" which are consistently good. The Chop Salad, Poppy Seed Fruit, and Mediterranean Salads all have chicken and are excellent healthy options.

The Chocolate Shakes are handmade with chocolate syrup. The Chocolate Cake Shake has, you guessed it, real chocolate cake in it. The Chocolate Cake is so good you will want it for your next birthday cake.

Before I get into this, know that they have the best Chicago dogs in the city. Period. And the best Italian Beef sandwiches. And the best wonton-style mozzarella sticks I've ever had. Even though my mother is toothless and in a nursing home, she still requests their Reubens every so often, and that's all she specifically asks for - they're that good.

I worked here 13-14 years ago, and had the pleasure of making every one of those things. I still eat there, if that means anything. Everything is exactly the same. Everything. Right down to the stainless tray with the slotted holes that we used to dump the fries into. The same old-school ketchup-colored tables kept spotless and disinfected, the same old-school Vienna glamor shots of the different types of hot dogs and sandwiches they make. The same picture of Mary, the owner's mother, above the serving window. I still remember the last time I got to hug her.

The owner, TJ, always was impeccable about cleanliness, and keeping his stuff in top shape - it was these things I held onto from working there. They are by far the cleanest restaurant I've ever worked in, even versus higher-end places like The Packing House I've been behind the scenes for. It's no less true where you can't see it as a customer. The back rooms are cleaner than the best-kept parts of your house - and TJ was never afraid to send someone back to clean something again if he felt it wasn't good enough. I know none of this has changed, either.

In fact, the only thing that has changed since I came in as a kid for the first time 28 years ago is that they took out the mini-golf that used to be in the back, some time before I put on the hat and shirt to work there. Might have been shortly after my best friend and I accidentally broke (and paid for) one of their putters...And they also now have a sleek tablet with a card reader.

This place is a landmark. It has timeless class and a deep seat in my heart - and stomach! The food is still exactly as I remember it 14 years ago, 28 years ago. It's rare that a restaurant keeps at what it's good at, and isn't tempted to get all flashy, trendy, and 'hip.' They've never changed the quality of the food to make more money. They didn't buy into the Sriracha or Chipotle-everything fads, they didn't have to 'buy into' the 'everything fresh' movement because they're already there. They perfected their work long ago, and it's great to see them keeping at it.

If you really love hot dogs, as well as A Chicago original, you can check out the Vienna Beef Factory Store and Deli.

Either purchase a hot dog and eat it inside the deli, or eat it outside under an umbrella, anything and everything you could possibility want to eat on or with it is available here.

Your can find some awesome deals on Vienna Beef merchandise, check out what's on sale for the best value.

The Vienna Beef History Museum opened on May 30, 2018 and I was told it will only be open to the public thru August of this year, 2018.

The museum is only open on weekdays from 10 am to 2 pm, so if you want to see it, go see it soon.

I could tell there was a problem with my mostaccoli order because they had to keep “checking” on the order in the back and while I ordered for pickup at 11am, I didn’t leave with all of my items until 11:25am.  It wasn’t the end of the world, but I got home with the food just as guests were arriving. Turns out, they forgot to include all the toppings for the hot dogs we ordered and I had nothing on hand but ketchup. :( it was really disappointing to place such a large order and not have everything you need and no time to run back. (It would have take me almost an hour out of the party time to run there and back)

I hate complaining and confrontation, but I did pop back into portillos the next day to pick up a free slice of chocolate cake as the birthday reward. I took the opportunity to at least give feedback in the catering area. I got an eye roll with the first gal I tried to tell what happened to, but she pulled in her manager and he looked up my order and quickly offered $ back to my order since I didn’t have the best experience. They didn’t have to do this, but I appreciate they did. If they hadn’t acknowledged the error at all I wouldn’t likely place another order - so well done, you made a catering customer this week! I’ll be back!

Tips for anyone ordering catering: make sure you open the boxes and check everything before you leave. I’ll probably ask the person working to do a full checklist and go through everything. Whether you still think of it as Red Hot Lovers or are making your first visit to town, this place is definitely worth a visit. Little local places with character are becoming harder to find. Not only is Ray's as good as my first visit a quarter century ago, it's even better today.

The interior has been updated without losing any of the charm. It's always spotless and it's quite common to see the staff cleaning the tiny little areas that are often neglected at other establishments. The fountain Coke here even tastes better (plus free refills) and I attribute it to the machine and nozzles being so well maintained.

More importantly, the passion for the food comes through with the attention and care given to the menu. Phil and the crew cut no corners when it comes to ingredients, authenticity, or preparation. Chicago dogs, Coneys, Cheesesteaks, Italian beef, pulled pork, waffle fries, etc. are all done right. The menu is small enough that they can master each item but large enough that you can come by more than once a week and still get nice variety.

Don't come in expecting fast food value menu pricing, because you'll certainly be receiving better quality. My lunch tab is usually around $10, but there are student and daily specials, along with some other nice options that are even more economical.

Jimmy's Red Hots in Chicago's Humboldt Park neighborhood is among the most iconic, Chicago-style hot dog destinations that not only continues to thrive, but has stayed true to the classic, 312 fixings and generous portions that many of us have come to love. I have even heard celebrities reference this place as their favorite Chi-Town dog in our Windy City.

Great value. Consistent flavor. Open for over 55 years. The only changes that I noticed in a decade are the slight increase in menu prices (on par with inflation) and the heat-insulated, carryout bags that keep the dog and the fries hot (WHICH ARE STILL A COMPLIMENTARY ACCOMPANIMENT LIKE THE OLD DAYS). Now every fast-food vendor sells fries a la carte and will charge you extra for additional condiments such as Tzatziki (cucumber sauce) for that authentically flavored Gyro.

To this day, I love that Jimmy's refuses to add ketchup, or catsup depending on your hometown, to any of their hot dogs. They have maintained this position as a form of divine doctrine. If you want ketchup, you are welcome to ask for some "for your fries," but be prepared to be shunned by locals and workers for such debauchery if caught.

Thank you for staying the same Jimmy! Every time I stop in for a dog, polish or gyro, your place takes me back 20 years because of the nostalgic flavor and aromas.

The food was prepared rather quickly.  The fries were great, crinkle cut and cooked to perfection with just the right amount of salt.  The chocolate cake shake was very rich.  It was hard to suck out of the straw due to the thickness of the chocolate cake.  That shake was no joke! Absolutely decadent! I could only have a few drinks before I'd had enough, which is strange, as I normally have an insatiable sweet tooth.  Now, the croissant.  After unwrapping it, the croissant was warm, but soggy and falling apart.  It didn't seem as though they had made an effort to toast it, to delay the onset of the sogginess.  I wasn't a huge fan of the "Italian beef," perhaps it is an acquired taste?  Nothing about the beef really spoke to me.  On the contrary, I had a difficult time getting it down.  It tasted bland and flavorless.

I did enjoy the dining experience, and my boyfriend swears by this place.  I will most likely be back, maybe giving their Chicago Dogs a try?

I was really pleased to see Portillos finally get opened up on the East side. It was delicious in all the ways we expected it to be. Let me clarify. If you've ever been to a Portillos and gotten an Italian beef, it's probably never dry bread, even if you don't get it dipped. Your food is probably never going to be ready in 30 seconds. That's not how Portillos works. What you can expect is pretty good crinkle cut fries, shakes that are great, though not great for you, and really solid burgers, beef and dogs. For people expecting it to be like other Portillos, great news: it is. For those expecting fine dining, it's not. It's Portillos. We went there at about 8:30 on a Wednesday night and it was slammed, like super slammed. The team was on point nonetheless and our food was as well. Italian beef, mine dipped with hot peppers, and great like I expected. Shakes and fries were good. Fries warm, not hot. And we waited maybe 3-4 minutes. It's not a super unique layout, follows the generic "retro 50s" feel they give the restaurants that don't get a special theme. Parking will be interesting but not a huge deal. If you haven't been yet, make the time. It will be worth it.

It's a drive-in diner that makes their own hot dogs (unlike the countless Vienna Beef or Red Hot Chicago joints) and they top their dogs with all the right toppings, stuff them in a box with fries made from potatoes they cut themselves (I literally saw the tubes of skinned potatoes coming off the truck during my visit). You have the option to eat inside, their outside tables, or you can order and eat from your parked car. It's a slice of Americana right here. Their shakes are delicious as well.

P.S. I've lived in and around Chicago since I was two and have preferred ketchup on my hotdogs. Every now and then I'll order it on my dog and I get no backlash from the cashier. They'll put it on for ya if you ask for it.

The Trick to the Fries - Why the Hot Dogs, Hamburgers, & Beef are So Good

Portillo’s has the best Chicago Style Hot Dogs, Italian Sausage, Italian Beef, hamburgers, fries, and salads. Nothing else comes close.

Here's why the hotdogs taste so good. Vienna Beef worked with Dick Portillo years ago to create these hot dogs that can only be found at Portillo’s. The flavor is great but when you bite in there is almost a crunch. They aren't soggy like other places.

Just the regular fries are great but here are the tricks. First for a bit more ask for the "cheese fries" with mild cheddar cheese to dip them in. You can also ask for the fries to be "well done" so that they have this great crunch to them. The best.

The hamburgers are so good because they are cooked over an open flame to have a cookout taste. The special Milano Buns are so good, not like anything you can buy at the store. The Bacon Cheeseburgers are amazing. The Italian Beef is served on real Milano Rolls.

Most locations also have "Barney's Ribs" which are consistently good. The Chop Salad, Poppy Seed Fruit, and Mediterranean Salads all have chicken and are excellent healthy options.

The Chocolate Shakes are handmade with chocolate syrup. The Chocolate Cake Shake has, you guessed it, real chocolate cake in it. The Chocolate Cake is so good you will want it for your next birthday cake.

Everything is fresh and clean. There is always a line but it moves fast. Great place to bring kids.

I have actually contemplated on eating at Portillo's Hot Dogs for a while now, but I kept putting it off. I used to drive my client here through the drive-thru, but never really stepped foot inside until now. After leaving my college campus, I figured why not because I had over an hour to spare before work.

My first impression was wow! This place looks amazing inside! From my perspective with what its interior consisted of, and the attire worn by the employees, it felt like a combination of a classy food court, and a junkyard, hehe. With the edition of its Portillo's and Barnelli's sides, it feels like two different choices of foods in one area similar to a food court. And need I explain its classy interior, and the attire worn by its employees? Classy! And I loved every bit of it.

Both, the Portillo's and Barnelli's sides consisted of different things, but overall you have the choice of salads, pastas, desserts, burgers, hot dogs and sandwiches. The funny thing about ordering was that it took me longer choosing my order versus actually receiving my order, which was the jumbo hot dog w/ fries and drink.

Every time I visited Portillo's with my client in the past, it always looked congested from the outside, but during this in-restaurant visit I noticed that there were plenty of seats and tables available inside. If I would have visited the inner restaurant sooner, I would have took notice of that. Parking is no issue because of the restaurant parking lot being shared with other businesses as well as having its own section, but there may be issues with finding that spot within a few feet of the restaurant depending on what time of the day you visit. I visited slightly after noon, and did not have any issues finding a parking spot near the door.

After eating that jumbo hot dog w/ fries and drink, I would love to bundle up and take a little nap, but unfortunately I have to go to work. In Hawaii that is referred to as the Kanak Attack, which is the feeling of intense laziness one gets from eating too much, hehe. With that, best believe your bottom dollar I will be returning to Portillo's. And besides, with what their menu consists of on either the Portillo's or Barnelli's side you cannot fail satisfying your taste buds.

*Take note of its daily features listed near the register on the Portillo's and Barnelli's charts.

When you're looking for home cooked meals, you expect to wait a few hours before granny and/or mom comes down with their aprons on for prepping until the whole house has the aroma of your favorite meal. Well, portillo's brings all that together with their variety of meals! My personal favorite is the "Big Beef" with sweet peppers and "extra sauce" (where they add more juice from the beef that's been simmering for hours) on the sandwich. Fries and onion rings are a great compliment I'd say! But then theres great choices like the chilly cheese dogs, charbroiled chicken sandwich and even their chopped salad! The atmosphere is very homely and big enough for a group of 20 to sit comfortably! I highly recommend going, especially for the price and the product that'll bring you to a home cooked meal ready in less than 10 minutes!

This place is so famous, I doubt anyone will even bother reading this or even if it matters. But I’ll add my 2 cents anyway. I don’t quite know where to begin. I have never been to a fast food establishment where every facet of it, from the food, service, cleanliness, and decor is so great that it should be the gold standard to be emulated by everyone else. I do not exaggerate when I say that this is by far the best fast food franchise that I have ever been to. This location is awesome. But they are all awesome. Every single one. Anyone wanting to get in the fast food business should study how this business is run. Every single thing on the menu is among the very best of that particular food. Burgers? Among the very best. Hot dogs? Probably THE best. Italian beef? Most definitely the ABSOLUTE best. Salads? Polish? Ribs? You name it, it is going to be on your Top 5 or higher list for fast food. And my goodness, boy does your order arrive fast!!! This is where Portillo’s  really shines and separates themselves from everyone else. They have developed a system that needs to be bottled and sold. At every location I have been to, every staff runs like a well oiled machine. Each crew member is dialed in and focused in carrying out their assignment. It’s like organized chaos. Everyone is moving, smiling, and getting people their food fast without missing a beat. And this is true whether you are ordering inside or going through the drive thru. Only at Portillo’s can you be in the drive thru wrapped around the building in a line a block long and get your food in what seems like 5 minutes or less. It’s truly something to be behold. Where and how they train their employees I don’t know, but other places need to take notice. They put all other restaurants that have a drive thru to shame. One would think that with as fast as they are getting your food, their service must be riddled with mistakes, right? Wrong! Their accuracy is astounding!!! In all the dozens and dozens of times I’ve been there, I have never ever been handed anything wrong with my order. When every time you go through the drive thru and turn to your wife to say how awesome this place is, your passion gets to the point where you have to express it. Thank you Portillo’s for being you.

The Dearborn area is loaded with an unreasonable number of outstanding burger places, and  I'm on a quest to try them all. We hit Taystee's at 9:15 on a Saturday night after a long evening of running errands.

It's inside one half of a BP convenience store, yes, but this is a new and very modern building, not a dingy old store from the 60s. It's clean, brightly-lit, and has quite a bit of seating. When we walked in, there were only a couple other customers, but the four guys behind the counter were hard at work putting together carryout orders- they do a lot of carryout business at night, as I saw.

We stood near the register and took about 8 minutes to decide what we wanted, but the cashier guy never once rushed us or asked if we were ready; I really appreciated that. Ordering was easy, and they had no problem with the substitutions I wanted to make on my burger. I got the Mac Attack burger, the GF got the pizza burger, and we got a basket of spicy fries to share. The burgers were $7.50 and $8, the fries were $3, so the bill was just under $20. (Sandwich prices range from $6-10.) The cashier asked if it was our first time there; when I said yes, he gave me a couple of fountain cups and said, "Here, these are on the house. We're glad you're here." VERY nice touch.

Shortly after we ordered, a wave of people came in to order. Our food took about 9-10 minutes to come out, which was fine. I sat and watched college football on their one TV. The food was all ready at the same time, and all hot.

Both burgers were great, though the pizza burger looked like the better of the two. (I can't tell you how it tasted, because she wolfed it down before I could even get a bite.) My Mac Attack was great too, though the fried mac&cheese balls didn't add as much flavor as I'd hoped. The burger patties themselves were perfectly cooked, the cheeses were melted, the veggies were the right balance between cooked and crunchy, and the brioche buns did a stellar job of holding it all together.

(Seriously, some of our metro's better-known restaurants need to take a damn note from Taystee's and use these buns instead of the flimsy, soggy, falling-apart Kroger buns that too many restaurant burgers are served on. I can't enjoy my burger if it's falling into my palm or onto my plate- or lap- and Taystee's has that figured out.)

The fries sucked- they were soggy and pretty dense to the tooth, indicating they were only about 85% cooked. Either the oil wasn't hot enough, or- more likely- they sat too long in the metal bowl being used to apply the spices/seasonings after frying. We each ate about three fries. Not a big loss, though- we took them home and will stick them in the oven for 10-15 minutes, and that should crisp them up with no problem. The staff was busy and working hard, and I understand that fries were being cooked in bulk, so I'm not taking a star off for that. If they do it every single time, I might knock off a star on future visits, but for now, they more than earned a free pass on something that small.

While I have plenty more Dearborn burgers to try, I already plan on going back to Taystee's. It's an awesome option at any time of day, but being open late in an area where so much is closed by 9:00pm is a great bonus. Go there!

The menu is wide and thoroughly excellent across all locations, and the decor varies between restaurants, but is always a very well done 30s-50s Americana theme, often very elaborate. Not quite fast food, but very, very close, but the food tastes like a much more traditional restaurant. Can be a bit dearly priced if you're comparing it to other drive through places, but the quality more than backs it up.

The interior of the restaurant has a bit of a dinner feel with the furniture and knick knacks. The ordering process is relatively quick - you walk up to the counter and place your order. There is a drive thru, but the wait is long if they are busy.
The staff is friendly and the setup allows you to watch as food is prepared.

You run into layers of flavor with the shake, some more chocolaty than others, but very tasty.

One word- authentic.  I've spent a lot of time in Chicago and as such I am familiar with the particulars of a Chicago-style hot dog.  Just a couple weeks ago I had a chance to catch the Cubs beat the Braves at Wrigley Field on a Monday- got a couple Chicago Dogs at the game and (ironically) they reminded me of Ann Arbor!  Real poppy-seed bun topped with sport peppers, tomato wedges and celery salt.  Neon green relish and diced onion, just the right amount of mustard, and a thick pickle spear.  Ray's pickles are even the New Pickles that haven't been in the brine very long- I've been looking for these for my home fridge and they're hard to find.  All of which leads me to believe Ray's takes the time to find the proper ingredients and do things right.  Add to this the fantastic (and genuinely friendly) customer service and the CCR on the speakers and you've got a recipe for my favorite hot dog joint in south-east Michigan.  Probably in the entire state.

I make sure that when I'm in Chicago, I stay in a hotel around Portillo's because it's that good.  Now, it IS a chain, it IS decorated to be super touristy, and I wouldn't try to pass this off as the best food in Chicago, there are plenty of other fine dining options that surpasses them.  What Portillo's brings to the table is a down to earth sandwich/hot dog that's as iconic as the Hancock building or the Sears/Willis tower.  Every city has "their" hot dog.  Seattle adds cream cheese and grilled onions, New York keeps it nice and simple, but Chicago dogs are by far my favorite with their hot peppers.

However for an even better time, nothing beats their Italian beef served with sweet or hot peppers, and if you like, served with cheese and/or their au jus (personal favorite: Italian beef, hot peppers, dipped).  If you're feeling extra hungry, go for either their Big Beef or Italian beef & sausage, you really can't go wrong.  Just know that whatever you get, it's a mess to eat, but it's just as much fun licking your fingers after.  I was in Chicago for a long weekend and ended up going back 3 times...not because there isn't other great food options in Chicago, but when I'm in the mood for a meal more for the common man, Portillo's is sure to hit the spot.

Fellow Yelper, Birdie M, a Yelper living on the west coast brought this location to my awareness. And after I pinpointed that its location was near my job, I made it my sole purpose to drive out after my work shift. I felt all giddy-like in anticipation once I saw its rooftop mascots prior to turning on N Milwaukee Ave. With its plain black exterior, it is the mascot characters on the rooftop that makes Superdawg Drive-In stand out amongst any other restaurant around. The restaurant reminds me of Sonic Drive-In with its drive-in set ups which is fitting to the times we are in with so many Covid-19 precautions at restaurants.

Ordering from their menu was a simple process; there was a button to press on the machine and the waitress responded immediately. I ended up ordering a superburger w/ fries and a drink because it appeared fitting for me as a first time visitor. But one particular item that kept catching my eye on the menu as well as pictures of it shared on Yelp was the whoopercheesie which I would definitely love to try on a different visit.

Within a reasonable time frame, the waitress, in good spirits came out with my order and took my payment. And oh my God, my food smelt like heaven once I received it and as I started putting together a review for this restaurant.

I loved the superburger! It had Chicago style relish on it, the same relish used on the Chicago style hot dog which gave it an amazing taste. Now the fries on the other hand I was not fond of. They were not fresh in comparison to the superburger, and had sort of a burnt taste to them. With these hot dog restaurants, the majority of the time it is the fries that give me something to look forward to, but for this one I will pass on the fries.

While bearing the taste of those fries, a highlight for me was seeing another customer hit one of the ordering machines with his beautiful Mercedes SUV. Instead of pulling in with the driver side at the ordering machine, he pulled in with his passenger side next to it which was very unorthodox. I could not resist chuckling at what I just saw, but I imagine that the driver has good insurance.

In closing, it was the taste of the superburger that honestly gave my taste buds something to yearn for, as well as the experience. I do know that fries can be a hit-or-miss at any restaurant, so I could not base my view and whether or not I return because of that after this visit. A great treat for the family or even friends to visit for lunch, dinner, or even late at night is Superdawg Drive-In.

The chicken sandwich was really great! The onion rings were of the crunchy breaded variety.... if your idea of onion rings is the classic, big beer-battered vibe, these are not that.

The malt was very thick, which some people love, and seemed to be made from soft serve ice cream rather than hand-dipped ice cream. Getting it through the straw is a nice challenge for the stout-hearted. Also the amount of malt powder used was such that if you had told me it was a regular milkshake, I would have believed you. So that was a bit of a disappointment. Next time I would definitely ask for extra malt powder. If you're going to have a malt you want to taste malty!  Can I get an amen from the back of the room?

Social distancing and keeping the tables clean and disinfected seemed to be a high priority, so it felt like a very safe environment.

I can say this about Portillo's - their food, for what it is, is not at all bad, but I've been now three times, and every time some small thing is wrong. It's either no napkins or a lacking ingredient or dressing/sauce packet. As it stands, there is nothing wrong with Chicago-style hot dogs at all, but tbh my preference remains Nathans or Hebrew National NY style with brown mustard, sauerkraut, relish and onions (red, if available). That being said, I do have to hand it to their Italian beef and sausage combo. That thing slays. My wife liked their chicken Caesar salad a lot, but was meh on the chicken sandwich. A staple of Vernon Hills and 1 of the more interesting Portillo's/Barnelli's locations with the 1920s car & speakeasy scene suspended over the main dining floor. You can walk in and stand in 1 line for Portillo's (italian beef, hot dogs, burgers, fish & chicken sandwiches, fries, milkshakes, cake, beer, etc) -OR- the line for Barnelli's (pasta, salad, etc.), but to order from both kitchens simultaneously, you'll need a 2nd person, otherwise you'll have to wait in line all over again. It gets pretty noisy inside so pay attention when they're calling out order numbers, if you don't respond on the 2nd or 3rd announcement, they set your order aside move on to customers who ARE ready for their food. Then it's up to you to get your food before someone else [accidentally] takes it. There is a drive through which works a little differently from other drive-throughs. Staff will walk between cars to write down orders and give you a Number (like a deli) then radio it in to the kitchen and wave you to pull up and keep the line moving. But it can also be noisy outside depending on the vehicles. And most of the drive-through staff are teenagers that will mess up the order so make you sure have their attention and see they wrote the right stuff. You CANNOT GET BARNELLI's (pastas) FROM THE DRIVE-THROUGH, only Portillo's food is available (even cake by the slice I think you have to go inside for).
My favorite dishes @ Barnelli's are the Chicken Carbonara, Alfredo, Baked Mostaccioli, and their Chop Salad.

We enjoyed our FREE meal at Portillo's, and are looking forward to eating here many, many more times. This Portillo's officially OPENS to the Public, Tuesday, January 31, 2017. They still need to work out some kinks, but all in all, we had a positive experience. On our way out, they handed us bags with a slice of their decadent and famous chocolate cake. This was a very nice touch which we appreciated. Welcome to the Neighborhood Portillo's!  We wish you many, many years of success. I predict that the Buona Beef across the street and down the block will not be around much longer. The quality of food at Portillo's is excellent. Their Italian beefs are legendary as are their hot-dogs. The bread is always fresh and perfect.  The choices at Portillo's and Barnelli's are endless. What is Portillo's? Coming from Chicago and experiencing the Portillo's craze for many years, it is always hard to describe what it is to new people. Oh it's just burgers, hot dogs, and italian beef is the response after describing it to the other people; however it is more than that. When Portillo's is done well, it is flame grilled burgers made fresh, it's crinkly fries with a cheese diping sauce, its the whole slice of cake blended in a milk shake. In Chicago, these locations always have a long drive thru line at all hours of the day. I can say when it is not done well such as at the one in Champaign, you get a lack luster experience. We recently came after a show at the Coliseum and I had the chopped salad instead of the flame grilled burger. The serving size was enormous. The noodles were cooked well with tons of blue cheese and bacon. So far I am impressed by the quality and the service as well. Will be back to try the famous italian beef or the italian beef combo!

There was a crazy line around the corner, even on a weekday afternoon, and I was given to understand that it's basically always been like this, although perhaps it's now a bit worse because of the imminent closure. The line moves decently quickly, though, and the process and seating are efficient, so (at least when it's warm enough to eat outside) people who want to dine in won't have to wait for a seat after ordering (their policy is that you don't sit until after you order).

The menu is impressive. You can pick your own sausage, preparation and toppings, or get a special (weekly, I think). The specials are gourmet and unusual, like Thai chicken or venison or escargot. You can have any sausage grilled (a clear choice), steamed, fried, or fried and grilled. You pick your toppings, from the basic Chicago dog toppings, with a bunch of other options. This seems like a place that wouldn't necessarily tolerate pickiness (the "take it or leave it" school of thought), but in fact they make it exactly to order, which is great and explains the wait.

Cash only really annoys me, and it's not just that this place has a minimum to charge, some people place big orders for lots of people, and it's still cash only. I think it shows a disconnect with customer preferences, and potentially shady behavior. But I can deal with it on occasion, and Doug's is up front about it at least. I didn't see an ATM, so I'd recommend having some cash on-hand before waiting in line, and count on $10 per person, since the specials and a drink and fries will run about that. The staff helped me to get over my annoyance because they were very friendly and calm despite the hectic setting, and food came quickly. It was very good (for a hot dog, bear in mind).

I biked, and there's a little bit of bike parking, but there could be more. There seemed to be plenty of free street car parking, especially because there's a lot of turnover.

Fellow Yelper, Birdie M, a Yelper living on the west coast brought this location to my awareness. And after I pinpointed that its location was near my job, I made it my sole purpose to drive out after my work shift. I felt all giddy-like in anticipation once I saw its rooftop mascots prior to turning on N Milwaukee Ave. With its plain black exterior, it is the mascot characters on the rooftop that makes Superdawg Drive-In stand out amongst any other restaurant around. The restaurant reminds me of Sonic Drive-In with its drive-in set ups which is fitting to the times we are in with so many Covid-19 precautions at restaurants.

Ordering from their menu was a simple process; there was a button to press on the machine and the waitress responded immediately. I ended up ordering a superburger w/ fries and a drink because it appeared fitting for me as a first time visitor. But one particular item that kept catching my eye on the menu as well as pictures of it shared on Yelp was the whoopercheesie which I would definitely love to try on a different visit.

Within a reasonable time frame, the waitress, in good spirits came out with my order and took my payment. And oh my God, my food smelt like heaven once I received it and as I started putting together a review for this restaurant.

I loved the superburger! It had Chicago style relish on it, the same relish used on the Chicago style hot dog which gave it an amazing taste. Now the fries on the other hand I was not fond of. They were not fresh in comparison to the superburger, and had sort of a burnt taste to them. With these hot dog restaurants, the majority of the time it is the fries that give me something to look forward to, but for this one I will pass on the fries.

While bearing the taste of those fries, a highlight for me was seeing another customer hit one of the ordering machines with his beautiful Mercedes SUV. Instead of pulling in with the driver side at the ordering machine, he pulled in with his passenger side next to it which was very unorthodox. I could not resist chuckling at what I just saw, but I imagine that the driver has good insurance.

In closing, it was the taste of the superburger that honestly gave my taste buds something to yearn for, as well as the experience. I do know that fries can be a hit-or-miss at any restaurant, so I could not base my view and whether or not I return because of that after this visit. A great treat for the family or even friends to visit for lunch, dinner, or even late at night is Superdawg Drive-In.

I make sure that when I'm in Chicago, I stay in a hotel around Portillo's because it's that good.  Now, it IS a chain, it IS decorated to be super touristy, and I wouldn't try to pass this off as the best food in Chicago, there are plenty of other fine dining options that surpasses them.  What Portillo's brings to the table is a down to earth sandwich/hot dog that's as iconic as the Hancock building or the Sears/Willis tower.  Every city has "their" hot dog.  Seattle adds cream cheese and grilled onions, New York keeps it nice and simple, but Chicago dogs are by far my favorite with their hot peppers.

However for an even better time, nothing beats their Italian beef served with sweet or hot peppers, and if you like, served with cheese and/or their au jus (personal favorite: Italian beef, hot peppers, dipped).  If you're feeling extra hungry, go for either their Big Beef or Italian beef & sausage, you really can't go wrong.  Just know that whatever you get, it's a mess to eat, but it's just as much fun licking your fingers after.  I was in Chicago for a long weekend and ended up going back 3 times...not because there isn't other great food options in Chicago, but when I'm in the mood for a meal more for the common man, Portillo's is sure to hit the spot.

Portillo's has a fun vibe, very Chicago and definitely brimming with a sense of their business history.  Plan on spending at least a few minutes just gawking around at everything that's hanging on the walls and ceiling, then another few minutes gawking at their food choices.

I would encourage you to look at their menu online so that you get a good idea of what to expect when you get there. I ended up choosing a chicken sandwich, onion rings and a chocolate malt. The chicken sandwich was really great! The onion rings were of the crunchy breaded variety.... if your idea of onion rings is the classic, big beer-battered vibe, these are not that.

The malt was very thick, which some people love, and seemed to be made from soft serve ice cream rather than hand-dipped ice cream. Getting it through the straw is a nice challenge for the stout-hearted. Also the amount of malt powder used was such that if you had told me it was a regular milkshake, I would have believed you. So that was a bit of a disappointment. Next time I would definitely ask for extra malt powder. If you're going to have a malt you want to taste malty!  Can I get an amen from the back of the room?

Social distancing and keeping the tables clean and disinfected seemed to be a high priority, so it felt like a very safe environment.

I'll definitely be back, although I will make different choices next time. I'm mystified by tamales being one of their side items. (??!!) Intrigued.

There was a crazy line around the corner, even on a weekday afternoon, and I was given to understand that it's basically always been like this, although perhaps it's now a bit worse because of the imminent closure. The line moves decently quickly, though, and the process and seating are efficient, so (at least when it's warm enough to eat outside) people who want to dine in won't have to wait for a seat after ordering (their policy is that you don't sit until after you order).

The menu is impressive. You can pick your own sausage, preparation and toppings, or get a special (weekly, I think). The specials are gourmet and unusual, like Thai chicken or venison or escargot. You can have any sausage grilled (a clear choice), steamed, fried, or fried and grilled. You pick your toppings, from the basic Chicago dog toppings, with a bunch of other options. This seems like a place that wouldn't necessarily tolerate pickiness (the "take it or leave it" school of thought), but in fact they make it exactly to order, which is great and explains the wait.

Cash only really annoys me, and it's not just that this place has a minimum to charge, some people place big orders for lots of people, and it's still cash only. I think it shows a disconnect with customer preferences, and potentially shady behavior. But I can deal with it on occasion, and Doug's is up front about it at least. I didn't see an ATM, so I'd recommend having some cash on-hand before waiting in line, and count on $10 per person, since the specials and a drink and fries will run about that. The staff helped me to get over my annoyance because they were very friendly and calm despite the hectic setting, and food came quickly. It was very good (for a hot dog, bear in mind).

The seating is a mixture of tables, booths, stools with a separate, small dining area (similar to the Portillo's on Dempster across the street from Lutheran General Hospital in Park Ridge, IL). We have lived in the area for over 23 years, so we were super stoked to see Portillo's go up in this area. It is located less than 1-block west of Harlem Ave. Take Lawrence Ave. (it is on the North side of Lawrence).  This location also has a Barnelli's (pasta and salads) as well as a drive-thru which is awesome. The parking lot is fairly large. We enjoyed our FREE meal at Portillo's, and are looking forward to eating here many, many more times. This Portillo's officially OPENS to the Public, Tuesday, January 31, 2017. They still need to work out some kinks, but all in all, we had a positive experience. On our way out, they handed us bags with a slice of their decadent and famous chocolate cake. This was a very nice touch which we appreciated. Welcome to the Neighborhood Portillo's!  We wish you many, many years of success. I predict that the Buona Beef across the street and down the block will not be around much longer. The quality of food at Portillo's is excellent. Their Italian beefs are legendary as are their hot-dogs. The bread is always fresh and perfect.  The choices at Portillo's and Barnelli's are endless. Portillo's has a decent price point for the quality and quantity of what they offer.

So I ended up with a very well done burger that was quite dry. I have to have a juicy burger for it to be any good. Also, they say it is 1/3 lb. before cooking. That didn't seem to be the case, but maybe because it had been in the broiler too long and lost all that weight and volume in lost juiciness. It did come with a nice thick slice of fresh tomato, lettuce, and onions. It would have been a good burger if the beef hadn't been so dry. I was expecting them to ask me how I wanted it and cooked it to order, but that isn't their business model. I don't mind waiting an extra 10 minutes, but I guess a lot of people want their food right away and that isn't practical. But now I know, no burgers for me from there anymore. Maybe they are better when they are busier because they are turning over faster? Also, I got a large order of fries which was actually enough to split with 2 people. The decor is old time Chicago, so we had plenty to take in visually while we waited for our food and while we ate it. It was noisier than other places, so we didn’t talk much. My husband heard our number called, and got our 3 hotdogs, large fries and drinks at the pick up area. It wasn’t a cheap dinner, but it wasn’t expensive either.

Our hot dogs were good. So were the fries. Nothing was overly greasy or overcooked. My husband is a big fan, and will go out of his way to enjoy a Portillo’s hot dog at home in Tampa. Tonight he relished his plain dogs in Chicago, the birthplace of Portillo’s. I enjoyed my meal, but it didn’t overwhelm me. So if you want a good hot dog and an order of fries, with lots of Chicago ambiance, then come to Portillo’s.

My first job was working for Portillo's when I was 16 years old. Back then, there were only 8 stores (long ago!). Over the years, I watched the company grow into the the large chain that exists today. On the plus side, the signature Italian beef sandwiches are the best around, and the dogs are way up there as well. That said, I have come to believe that these restaurants are highly overrated. The prices are inflated, and these guys don't give anything away for free...no coupons (ever!), no drink refills, nada. No wonder Dick got so wealthy...good for him. But, in my humble opinion, the quality of the food (frozen burger patties!) overall does not justify the high pricing, waiting in line for 20+ minutes, or sitting in the drive through line, which often extends around the building...only to be told to go park and wait longer before driving away with a little pink number tag that they put under your windshield wiper. For me, this is a once in a while place at best.

It may be silly to write this review so soon before Hot Dougs is closing for good, but I figure I'd speak my piece in case there are any other folks who have never been (like myself) and plan to hit up the place before it closes for good October 3rd.

I've been wanting to try Hot Dougs for years, and since it's closing in less than a month I figured it was time to hightail it over there. Like most normal folk, I'm not super keen on long lines, though I don't mind putting in a little pain for ultimate gain every once in a while, and that's what I was expecting in this scenario.

After a 45 minute wait on a Wednesday afternoon, we finally get inside. It's adorable. The specialty hot dog lists all sound crazy impressive. It's cash only, and only had enough money for four (between 2 of us), so it was a tough call but we decided on the famous fois gras dog, the lamb curry, the jack daniels and fennel, and the escargot. I was stoked city.

After everything was served and done, however....I was...underwhelmed. The fois gras dog (while I totally appreciate it's eff-you fois gras ban origins) was a little too much of the same rich taste with little balance. I took a bit of each other dog, and while some were better than others (lamb curry and escargot being mah favs) it was just sort of disappointing. I was expecting to want to stuff my face, and I had a hard time eating even slightly past full. I boxed up my leftover dogs and headed home, saddened by what had become a 2 1/2 hour field trip.

That said...HERE is how you should eat Hot Dougs if you decide to go:

-Get a shitton of specialty hot dogs to go.
-Go home, and put all of them in the fridge except for what you want to eat now
-put that dog in the oven for like 10 minutes on 350 (and do just about the same with the others when you cook them, maybe a tiny bit higher and longer if they are cold) - the bun gets all toasty and the cheese gets all melty...It was like a night and day eating experience.

I did this with my leftovers the next morning (today) and decided that was worth standing in line for. So...if you MUST to avoid feeling like you missed out on a Chicago classic...do that.

The menu offerings at the VH location are "good" as long as you actually get the food that you order. If you have a hankering for hot dogs, uber crispy panko crusted onion rings, Italian beef, fries, etc., Portillo's will satisfy those cravings. However, what I will stress is that it is IMPERATIVE to check your order "before" you leave the premises. This is especially critical when ordering via drive-thru.
If a menu item is ordered with additions or modifications, it is extremely important to check the entire sandwich to ensure the request was actually fulfilled. For take-out and drive-thru, it is no longer enough to perform just a visual piece count of your order.
In my experiences via the drive-thru, EACH and EVERY time that I have ordered the "Hotdog with Everything + ketchup" my order has been wrong. Each and every time, what I receive is a hotdog with ONLY ketchup. "Everything" plus ketchup is vastly different from a hotdog "ONLY" ketchup. The receipt lists it correctly, therefore the order taker understands the request however, once it reaches the kitchen, somehow the wheels fall clean off the bus. Between items not making it into the bag at all, or items not being prepared to specification, I have just a tad bit of frustration with this location. And what ever happened to QAing the orders before passing them off to the customer?

Overall, the food is fresh, fast and tasty, however as it pertains to order prep & execution, attention to detail, and overall accuracy & consistency, there is definitely room for extensive and immediate improvement.

Portillo's is an institution, but one that now rests too much on its laurels.  It is neither what it once was, nor what it ought to be.

To begin with, the good:  The burgers, Italian beef, and hot dogs are all solid.  And the crinkle-cut french fries are a great accompaniment in pretty much every case.

The not-so-good:  Portillo's service has, in recent visits, been slow and inattentive.  Lackadaisical.  Order-takers fail to ask pertinent questions and fail properly to record orders.

There are no kids options, no kids meals.  A real demerit for a presumably family-friendly joint.

Some items are grossly over-priced.  My seven-year-old daughter ordered a fruit cup at $3.99.  She gets an 8-ounce plastic cup containing apple slices and a single sliced strawberry.  (I watched them making it.)  Ridiculous.

On the Italian beefs.  Some of us like to order them dry with plenty of gravy on the side.  Some places -- Buona for example -- understand this, and will give you gravy in a bowl.  Smart.  Portillo's hands you these Dixie-cup-sized things that aren't made for dipping . . . AT ALL.  Again, poor form, Portillo's.

Not only that, but, for goodness sake, people, how about you relocate the soft drink dispensers to the CUSTOMER side of the counter?!?!?!  This must be another of Portillo's poorly-conceived nods to tradition or something.

In short, Portillo's could take a number of very modest adjustments to restore it's position as a top option.  But, until then, it is lucky it does not get only two stars.

For me, this is a once in a while place at best.

Portillo's is an institution, but one that now rests too much on its laurels.  It is neither what it once was, nor what it ought to be.

To begin with, the good:  The burgers, Italian beef, and hot dogs are all solid.  And the crinkle-cut french fries are a great accompaniment in pretty much every case.

The not-so-good:  Portillo's service has, in recent visits, been slow and inattentive.  Lackadaisical.  Order-takers fail to ask pertinent questions and fail properly to record orders.

There are no kids options, no kids meals.  A real demerit for a presumably family-friendly joint.

Some items are grossly over-priced.  My seven-year-old daughter ordered a fruit cup at $3.99.  She gets an 8-ounce plastic cup containing apple slices and a single sliced strawberry.  (I watched them making it.)  Ridiculous.

On the Italian beefs.  Some of us like to order them dry with plenty of gravy on the side.  Some places -- Buona for example -- understand this, and will give you gravy in a bowl.  Smart.  Portillo's hands you these Dixie-cup-sized things that aren't made for dipping . . . AT ALL.  Again, poor form, Portillo's.

Not only that, but, for goodness sake, people, how about you relocate the soft drink dispensers to the CUSTOMER side of the counter?!?!?!  This must be another of Portillo's poorly-conceived nods to tradition or something.

In short, Portillo's could take a number of very modest adjustments to restore it's position as a top option.  But, until then, it is lucky it does not get only two stars.

Ok, first of all I did not order a hot dog which is their claim to fame, but I was not impressed with this place overall.  Everything is separate here so the price of each item adds up quickly, even if reasonable at first.  For a burger, small fries and small drink you will pay a little over $8.  The burger is a nice size but I can either get more food for the same price or a cheaper burger somewhere else.  You can save money on the drink by ordering a water but the cup is small and you will be refilling it a lot.  Also, there are no kids size meals.  First time I have been to a "new" restaurant that doesn't offer smaller/cheaper portions for kids.  For that reason I would not call this place family friendly (it will blow your meal budget out of the water), especially little kid friendly.  They do have high chairs and booster seats, but you are probably going to have to over spend just to feed everyone what they want/like.  Kids sharing meals is possible if they like the same thing and are not big eaters but adult and kid sharing will probably leave the adult a bit hungry (even with a 1 yr old).

There is a large menu with a wide variety of options so I am sure there are some unique choices that are good.  However, if your family is just a burger/chicken/fries type of group I would definitely recommend going elsewhere because it's just too expensive and nothing special for what you get.  I even tried a pasta bowl and while good, I felt I would get more for my money down the road at Olive Garden.  Overall, food was good but over priced.  For one or two adults going out to eat here will probably not be a big deal and they would probably enjoy it.  This is not a good place to take a family with 2+ little kids, especially if you are budget conscious.

Also, I recommend knowing what you plan to order before you arrive.  The counter ordering experience is hectic, much easier if you have a game plan.

You walk in and it is a daunting task to figure out how and where to stand in line.  I counted at least eight different lines and they all seemed to go in three directions simultaneously.  Confusion.  I walked to the far right and stood in line.  There is a staffer waiting to take your order.  She was standing about 10 feet from the register.  You take the order the order taker took and you hand it to the cashier.  She confirms the the order.  Not sure why the two-step process, but ok, it is putting people to work.

Then it is a mad dash to get a table.  Tables everywhere, but none available.  You are eyeballing hot dogs covered in chili and cheese and half-eaten pickles on soaked napkins to see who will be ready to go.  You look at feet and knees and hips.  You are ready to pounce on the next available seat.  You don't care that it is dirty.  You spot the tourist.  They are frantically zipping and unzipping, folding and unfolding, and patting themselves down.  They are ready to leave.  They might need another minute.  Meanwhile the table with the locals, or so they appear, cleanly throw all their used paper goods into the bag that had their order written on it.  They wipe the table and before the last person in their party stands...I sit in an available chair as though the music had just stopped and I get to stay in the game a little longer.

Order numbers are called out.  It feels more like an auction house than anything else.  Numbers are being called, yelled really, into a microphone and out of speakers that were set too loud too long ago.  While you wait for your number to be be screamed out you stop and look around.  Two restaurants seem to share this address.  Or is it three restaurants.

The sports memorabilia lines the walls.  Chicago Pride on display.  You can google the various "art" that hangs here.  I won't bore you with it.  Let's just say that all three major sports are represented.  The decor seems disney-lite and the sports-stuff seems as though displayed by a hoarder.  To each his own.  To. Each. His. Own.

Was that my number?!??!

You take the order the order taker took and you hand it to the cashier.  She confirms the the order.  Not sure why the two-step process, but ok, it is putting people to work.

Then it is a mad dash to get a table.  Tables everywhere, but none available.  You are eyeballing hot dogs covered in chili and cheese and half-eaten pickles on soaked napkins to see who will be ready to go.  You look at feet and knees and hips.  You are ready to pounce on the next available seat.  You don't care that it is dirty.  You spot the tourist.  They are frantically zipping and unzipping, folding and unfolding, and patting themselves down.  They are ready to leave.  They might need another minute.  Meanwhile the table with the locals, or so they appear, cleanly throw all their used paper goods into the bag that had their order written on it.  They wipe the table and before the last person in their party stands...I sit in an available chair as though the music had just stopped and I get to stay in the game a little longer.

Order numbers are called out.  It feels more like an auction house than anything else.  Numbers are being called, yelled really, into a microphone and out of speakers that were set too loud too long ago.  While you wait for your number to be be screamed out you stop and look around.  Two restaurants seem to share this address.  Or is it three restaurants.

The sports memorabilia lines the walls.  Chicago Pride on display.  You can google the various "art" that hangs here.  I won't bore you with it.  Let's just say that all three major sports are represented.  The decor seems disney-lite and the sports-stuff seems as though displayed by a hoarder.  To each his own.  To. Each. His. Own.
